components.title: Sterling workbench
components.description: The Sterling workbench image that a hosted site runs for each person.

control-implementations.description: What the Sterling workbench's unit tests, in the workbench package's report, show about its hosted session.

implemented-requirements.description: Secrets an extension saves go to the person's own OpenBao path, never to memory.

statements.description: In a hosted session the workbench rebinds Theia's key store, through which its extensions keep their secrets, to a store that writes, reads, lists and deletes them under the person's own OpenBao KV path (kv/data/users/<entity id>/<service>/<account>) with the session's own OpenBao token. With no active session every call is refused and OpenBao is not called, and an OpenBao refusal or silence becomes a plain sentence that holds no secret, token or entity id. On a single computer the store is the system keyring; when the keyring cannot load, saving fails, and Theia's in-memory store is never used.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the site's OpenBao with the per-person KV policy and decides which secrets people may keep there.

implemented-requirements.description: The person's long-term keys stay in OpenBao.

statements.description: The workbench's key service signs with the person's long-term key only through OpenBao Transit: it logs in to OpenBao's step-up role with the forwarded sign-in token, signs with that token and then revokes it, and keeps no step-up token between signatures. It refuses without any OpenBao call when the token's acr is not the site's step-up value or its auth_time is missing, older than the step-up window or in the future. OpenBao makes and unwraps the person's data keys with their own key-encryption key, using the session token. In local mode none of these long-term keys is available.
statements.remarks: Your organization enrols each person's keys in the site's OpenBao and sets the step-up window.

implemented-requirements.description: A session acts only for the person it was started for.

statements.description: In a hosted session the workbench backend logs in to OpenBao with the forwarded sign-in token only when the token's email, the forwarded email header and the person the session was started for agree, ignoring case; on any disagreement it makes no login and shows that the sign-in check failed. Once active, a token or email header naming someone else is ignored. It renews its OpenBao token at half of each lease, revokes the token when the session stops, and puts no token or entity id in its status or its log lines.
statements.remarks: Your organization's Keycloak signs the person in; Theia Cloud starts one session per person.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench backend reaches only the addresses your organization configured.

statements.description: A request the workbench backend makes on behalf of its browser page, through Theia's backend request facade, may reach only the addresses your organization configured: the Open VSX address and the hosts of the model servers, as exact scheme, host and port patterns with no wildcard. With neither set the allow list is empty. Plain http is accepted only to a loopback model server, and a model server setting that is not a JSON list of addresses is refused with a sentence naming the setting.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the site's model servers and Open VSX address, and the site network policy limits egress for every pod.

implemented-requirements.description: Session pods run Node with the FIPS provider on a FIPS host.

statements.description: On the running site, the signed evidence export samples session pods and counts those where Node reports its FIPS provider on; the deployment collector passes only when every sampled session reports it. The OpenSSL FIPS provider of the RHEL 9 base is the module of CMVP certificate #5573, recorded with its approved-mode caveat in the dated hosted verification records.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the site's nodes in FIPS mode and produces the evidence export at least weekly.

control-implementations.description: Statements about the Sterling workbench from the 44.1 coverage work (44.1-14), from the workbench package's tests.

implemented-requirements.description: A hosted workbench session acts only for its own person: it logs in to OpenBao only when the sign-in agrees, and reads and writes only that person's secrets.

statements.description: A hosted workbench session acts only for its own person. Its backend logs in to OpenBao with the forwarded sign-in token only when the token's email, the forwarded email header and the session's user agree; when they disagree the session fails with no login. Once active, a token or header naming someone else is ignored. The person's secrets are kept only under their own entity's path, a guest's only under the guests space, and a path is refused for an entity id that is not a UUID. CI tests of the workbench prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who may use the workbench, through its sign-in service and Theia Cloud, and grants OpenBao roles to the sessions.

implemented-requirements.description: Requests the workbench backend makes for its page may reach only the addresses the site settings allow.

statements.description: Requests that the workbench backend makes for its browser page reach only the addresses its settings give: one exact pattern per model server host and port, and the Open VSX address when one is set, never a wildcard. Unset or empty settings allow nothing, a setting that is not a JSON array of strings is refused naming the setting, and Theia allows exactly the patterns the settings gave. CI tests of the egress contribution prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the model servers and the Open VSX address for its site, and enforces information flow on its own network.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench uses the person key only after a fresh step-up, through a short-lived token, and issues credentials only within an officer's role.

statements.description: The workbench gives each action only the access it needs. Signing with the person's long-term key logs in to OpenBao's step-up role after a fresh step-up, signs with that token and then revokes it; unwrapping a data key uses the session token and needs no step-up. A credential is issued only by an officer whose role covers its type, within the role's ceiling and before the role ends, and an agent or an unattended run cannot issue, revoke or list anything. CI tests of the key service and the issuer service prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization assigns the officer roles and the OpenBao policies, and reviews who holds them.

implemented-requirements.description: Only officers run the privileged credential and guest-secret functions, each after a fresh step-up.

statements.description: The workbench keeps its privileged functions from people without the role: issuing a credential needs the matching officer role within its ceiling, and listing or removing an ended guest's secrets needs a fresh step-up, with OpenBao refusing anyone who is not an officer and a non-officer seeing nothing. CI tests of the issuer and guest-secret services prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who holds the officer roles.

implemented-requirements.description: A workbench session's access to OpenBao ends when its sign-in tokens expire or the session stops.

statements.description: A hosted workbench session holds its OpenBao access only while its sign-in lasts: a refused renewal logs in again once with the latest unexpired token, and when every forwarded token has expired the session fails as token-missing. Stopping an active session revokes its token. CI tests of the session identity prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the sign-in and session lifetimes in its sign-in service and Theia Cloud.

implemented-requirements.description: Stopping a workbench session revokes its OpenBao token.

statements.description: When a hosted workbench session stops, its OpenBao token is revoked once and the session ends; a revoke that fails or times out still ends the session, and the step-up token used for a signature is revoked after it signs. CI tests of the session identity and the key service prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization ends sessions at its sign-in service and Theia Cloud when a person signs out or leaves.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench binds its session to the signed-in person and answers the activity tracker only with the session secret.

statements.description: The workbench keeps its session bound to the person who signed in: once active, a token or email header naming someone else is ignored and never replaces the latest token. The activity tracker's endpoint answers only exactly "Bearer" followed by the session secret, and anything else gets 401. CI tests of the session identity and activity prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization runs the sign-in service and the proxy that forward the person's token to the session.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench backend reaches OpenBao and remote model servers only over https, trusting the site's CA.

statements.description: The workbench backend talks to OpenBao and to remote model servers only over https: plain http is accepted only to a loopback address, and the OpenBao client trusts the CA in the site's CA file, without which a call cannot reach OpenBao. CI tests of the OpenBao client and the egress settings prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization issues the site's certificates and CA, and runs TLS on its OpenBao and model servers.

implemented-requirements.description: Documentation pages in the workbench are rendered without scripts or remote content.

statements.description: The workbench renders its bundled documentation without mobile code: a raw HTML block keeps its picture and text but never its scripts, handlers or remote sources, a mermaid diagram is drawn to an inline SVG that loads nothing, and an image from another address becomes a note. CI tests of the documentation renderer prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which other content and extensions its sessions may run.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench asks for a fresh step-up sign-in before it signs with the person key.

statements.description: Before it signs with the person's long-term key, the workbench requires a fresh step-up sign-in: the token's assurance (acr) must be the one the site configured and its sign-in time recent and not in the future, or the signature is refused with the fix and OpenBao is not called. On a site with no step-up assurance configured, signing is not set up. CI tests of the key service prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization configures the step-up assurance and window in its sign-in service and the site settings.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench keeps OpenBao tokens and secrets out of its errors and output.

statements.description: The workbench keeps the authenticators it handles out of sight: an OpenBao refusal or silence becomes a plain sentence with no secret, token or entity id; error texts name the method, the path with the person's id hidden, and the status, never a header or a body; and the site evidence collector's OpenBao token never appears in output, the ConfigMap or an error, and is revoked before the run ends. CI tests of the key store, the OpenBao client and the collector prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization protects the tokens and keys of its site in OpenBao and its sign-in service.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench checks the inputs its services take and refuses what it does not expect.

statements.description: The workbench checks what its services are given: a message to sign that is not base64 or is over 64 KiB is refused without a call, a secret path refuses a string with an unpaired surrogate and a name the encoding could not have made, and an OpenBao answer over 1 MiB or with invalid JSON is a bad response. CI tests of the key service, the secret paths and the OpenBao client prove these checks.
statements.remarks: Your organization validates what its own systems send to the workbench.

implemented-requirements.description: The workbench's errors are plain sentences without secrets, tokens, headers or bodies.

statements.description: The workbench's errors say what failed without exposing anything: OpenBao error texts name the method, the path with the person's id hidden and the status, never a header or a body, and a refusal or silence from the secret store becomes a plain sentence with no secret, token or entity id. CI tests of the OpenBao client and the key store prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who at its site may read the workbench's logs.

implemented-requirements.description: An ended guest's secrets are removed only after retention, by an officer, with a record.

statements.description: The workbench removes an ended guest's secrets only after their retention: it offers only disabled guests past retention with no removal record, refuses a guest enabled again, one not past retention, a staff entity or a malformed record before any delete, records who removed them once, and then deletes every secret of that guest and nothing of anyone else. CI tests of the guest-secret service prove these rules.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets the retention period and decides when a guest's access ends.

control-implementations.description: Supply-chain statements generated from the component inventory. Do not edit by hand: run node compliance/src/cli.ts supply-chain-statements --write.

implemented-requirements.description: Generated from the component inventory: its resources are reviewed and pinned before use.

statements.description: These resources of Sterling workbench each have a reviewed register entry with their licence, compliance fit and conditions, and are pinned as the component inventory lists them: npm package @theia/core 1.77.0, npm package @theia/editor 1.77.0, npm package @theia/filesystem 1.77.0, npm package @theia/monaco 1.77.0, npm package @theia/navigator 1.77.0, npm package @theia/plugin-ext-vscode 1.77.0, npm package @theia/preferences 1.77.0, npm package @theia/terminal 1.77.0, npm package @theia/workspace 1.77.0, npm package @theia/cli 1.77.0 (build only), npm package beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 (build only), npm package markdown-it 14.3.3 (build only) and npm package @near-ai/sterling-workbench-extension 0.1.0 (this repository's own code). The compliance fit check over the whole repository, run as a CI test, fails when one of them has no reviewed entry, is marked as not fitting, or is an image without a sha256 digest or an action without a full commit SHA.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects and accepts its suppliers and runs its own supply-chain risk management plan.
